title: Regional spillover throttling and residency-aware routing playbook for dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers running Dedicated capacity across multiple zones and regions require predictable throughput guarantees while also enforcing data residency constraints. Current failover behavior floods neighboring pools when capacity is constrained, which risks violating residency policies or creating unpredictable latency/cost spikes. This ticket designs and implements a combined solution: a regional spillover throttling mechanism, residency-aware routing policy, and autoscaler integration to preserve throughput SLOs without breaking data residency agreements.

Goals: 1) Enforce per-customer residency constraints (soft and hard) at routing time so no user traffic leaves authorized zones unless explicitly allowed. 2) Provide graceful spillover with throttles and prioritized queues so failover doesn't overwhelm adjacent pools. 3) Integrate with autoscaling to prewarm and allocate capacity when spillover is anticipated, preserving minimum throughput for high-tier commitments. 4) Produce an operational playbook (runbook) for emergency cross-zone fails and resident-data audits.

Scope and non-goals: Implement routing + throttle + autoscaler hooks for Dedicated fleets only. Does not change public API semantics or hosted API defaults. Does not implement billing changes (handled by PM follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Routing layer rejects cross-residency requests unless customer has explicit cross-region allowance flag
Spillover throttle applies token-bucket per-origin and per-destination pool and prevents >30% request surge to any fallback pool within 60s
Autoscaler exposes a prewarm API that can be triggered by the routing policy with a 120s lead time and honors reserved-capacity commitments
Runbook updated with step-by-step failover mitigation including metrics to watch and rollback criteria
E2E test harness simulating zone failure demonstrates <5% request loss for P0 customers with reserved throughput, and bounded latency increase
comments: 2026-03-02 — initial design sync: agreed on two residency modes: HARD (block) and SOFT (allow with audit and throttling). Action: eng to prototype routing-level residency checks.

2026-03-04 — architecture review (PM/Infra/Runtime): suggested adding per-customer spillover priority lanes (e.g., reserved, standard, best-effort). Decision: implement three priority classes and map customer commitments to lanes.

2026-03-06 — runtime notes from Ivan (runtime): KV cache warming required for prewarm signals; added 'prewarm-ready' handshake to autoscaler API. Follow-up: add a lightweight artifact ping to avoid full model load for short prewarm windows.

2026-03-08 — security review requested: residency audit trail must be stored in customer audit logs and exportable for compliance. Security Q: retention and encryption. TODO: coordinate with security & compliance team for KMS policy.

2026-03-10 — spike completed: prototype throttle enforced via token-bucket on the request router, with metrics exposed (throttle_rate, spillover_count, target_pool_util). Observed spillover smoothing under synthetic failure.

2026-03-12 — code review feedback from Lina (infra): prefer soft-fail telemetry tag 'residency_override=soft' instead of boolean to surface in traces. Also requested integration test that simulates cross-region legal hold header.
2026-03-12 — next: implement audit export + add canary deployment to staging region. Coordinate with PM for customer-facing docs and SLA language changes.
